slides.presenter_notes: Welcome everyone. content.title: Client Brief
content.body:
Ein Abayaa is a Saudi premium modest fashion brand with a dual-tier architecture serving the modern Saudi woman — from daily wear to Eid celebrations.

Three distinct lines: AZAL (everyday, SAR 300-515), Core Ein Abayaa (accessible premium, SAR 300-500), and Maison Ein (elevated luxury, SAR 514-795),...

slides.presenter_notes:
Ein Abayaa is not a startup — they have 151 products, nearly 2,000 variants, 31.8K Instagram followers, and a brand identity that resonates. What they lack is the direct response infrastructure to convert that attention into revenue. The dual-tier architecture — AZAL for everyday and Maison Ein for premium — is a competitive advantage no other Saudi abaya brand has. The Zid migration is the catalyst that unlocks everything else. Collections include Summer Shade, Season of Blossoms, AZAL, and Maison Ein.

[Full detail]: plus under-abaya dresses (SAR 350-450). Platform: Salla → Zid (migration in progress).

The brand has the raw ingredients; the strategy provides the conversion infrastructure.

content.title: Strengths
strengths: Dual-tier brand architecture (AZAL + Maison Ein) that no competitor replicates
Under-abaya dress category (SAR 350-450) with zero competitive pressure
14 active Meta ads with bilingual storytelling — more sophisticated than any competitor

slides.presenter_notes: The brand has strong visual identity, proven viral capability on TikTok (1.1M views), and already-sophisticated ad creative running for 5+ months. The unique dual-tier architecture bridges accessible premium and aspirational luxury — AZAL for everyday elegance at SAR 300-515, and Maison Ein for elevated occasions at SAR 514-795. Summer Shade 2026 collection has premium shell-inspired design language, 10-color palette, and rich storytelling material ready for marketing. BNPL via Tabby and Tamara is already active. Additional points: Two distinct visual aesthetics (red theatrical Maison Ein + white studio editorial) — recognizable brand world.

content.title: Weaknesses
weaknesses: Zero customer reviews on store — Sadal has 82+ per product, creating a massive trust gap
No email capture, no WhatsApp button, no abandoned cart recovery — zero retention infrastructure
BNPL per-installment amounts not displayed on product pages

slides.presenter_notes: The current Salla store lacks video hero, collection stories, rich product descriptions, and variant options. The Zid migration addresses this but critical CRO gaps remain. No stock-level urgency indicators, no social proof widgets, no size quiz for guided selling. TikTok following at 6.5K significantly lags Instagram at 31.8K — representing an untapped growth channel. Our 90-day strategy bridges these infrastructure gaps. The Zid migration is the foundation, and everything else builds on top of it. Additional points: All 14 active ads still link to old Salla store — must switch to Zid at launch.
Let us now look at the biggest challenges Ein Abayaa faces — and more importantly, how each challenge represents a clear opportunity.

content.title: Challenge 1: The Trust Gap
content.headline: Customers cannot feel fabric, verify sizing, or read reviews before committing SAR 300-795 online
bullets: Top 3 purchase barriers: sizing uncertainty, fabric-feel anxiety, color accuracy concerns
Zero visible customer reviews vs Sadal's 82+ per product
At mid-premium pricing, trust is the conversion bottleneck

slides.presenter_notes: This is the most critical challenge. When a Saudi woman is considering spending 450 riyals on an abaya online, she needs confidence. Sizing uncertainty is the number one barrier — every brand's sizing is different. Fabric feel is second — the fabric looks nice in photos but what about reality? And then color accuracy — will the color match what she sees on screen? Sadal has solved this with 82+ reviews per product. We need to build a comparable trust system, but at the premium level — not through discounting, but through content and social proof. A customer comparing a SAR 450 Ein Abayaa piece against a SAR 219 Sadal abaya with 82 five-star reviews will choose Sadal unless Ein Abayaa can match or exceed that social proof infrastructure. No competitor in the mid-premium tier (SAR 400-800) has invested in reviews — building the category's best trust system would be a decisive competitive advantage. Opportunity: Build the mid-premium tier's best trust infrastructure — reviews, UGC, size guides, fabric education.

content.title: The Retention Opportunity
content.label: WhatsApp open rate in Saudi Arabia
content.sublabel: 25% abandoned cart recovery documented for a Saudi women's wear label
content.context: Yet Ein Abayaa has zero retention marketing infrastructure — every lost visitor is permanently lost.

slides.presenter_notes: Here is the math that matters most. If we drive 10,000 visitors to the Zid store and convert 2.5%, that is 250 purchases. But 9,750 visitors leave without buying. Right now, zero of those 9,750 people hear from Ein Abayaa again. With abandoned cart recovery via WhatsApp — which has 98% open rates in Saudi Arabia — a Saudi women's wear label recovered 25% of abandoned carts. Email flows generate 30 times higher revenue per recipient than campaigns. Building this infrastructure before scaling paid spend is non-negotiable. Fashion e-commerce cart abandonment rates run at 70-80% globally, meaning Ein Abayaa is losing 97-98% of its traffic with no mechanism to bring them back.

Email automated flows generate 30x higher revenue per recipient than campaigns

slides.presenter_notes: Across the entire Saudi abaya market, no competitor shows evidence of sophisticated retention marketing — no welcome flows, no abandoned cart sequences, no post-purchase nurture. This is a category-wide gap. For Ein Abayaa, this means every website visitor who does not purchase on their first visit is effectively lost. With fashion e-commerce cart abandonment rates at 70-80% globally, and an estimated 2-3% conversion rate, Ein Abayaa is losing 97-98% of its traffic with no mechanism to bring them back. The data is clear on the impact. These channels represent the highest-leverage investment in the entire strategy. Opportunity: WhatsApp (98% open rate) + email automation (30x flow RPR) = highest-leverage investment.

content.title: A Homogeneous Ad Landscape
content.label: Active Meta abaya ads in KSA
content.sublabel: Every single one uses product-catalog format. Zero brand storytelling.
content.context: Ein Abayaa already runs 14 ads more sophisticated than any competitor — but UGC, retargeting, and BNP...

slides.presenter_notes: This was the most surprising finding in our research. We scanned 590+ active abaya ads on Meta in Saudi Arabia. Every single one looks the same: product photo or video, fabric type, cut description, order now. That is it. No one tells a brand story. No one uses customer try-on content. No one runs retargeting ads with social proof or urgency. Ein Abayaa is already ahead — their ads use bilingual storytelling. But we can push much further with UGC, collection narratives, and retargeting creative. In a homogeneous landscape, differentiation wins.

slides.presenter_notes: Our Meta Ad Library scan revealed a remarkable finding: across 590+ active abaya ads in Saudi Arabia, every single ad uses the same format — product number, fabric type, cut description, and 'Order Now' CTA. No brand runs story-driven creative. No brand uses UGC customer try-on content in paid ads. No brand deploys retargeting-specific creative addressing objections. Ein Abayaa already runs 14 active Meta ads that are more sophisticated than any competitor — using bilingual storytelling copy and brand narrative. But they still have not deployed UGC, retargeting creative, or BNPL-focused ad copy. The opportunity is wide open.

content.title: A Massive Market, Accelerating
content.label: Saudi e-commerce market size in 2026
content.context: Fashion is a primary B2C growth driver. Online sales expected to exceed SAR 100 billion in 2026.

slides.presenter_notes: The Saudi e-commerce market is massive and accelerating. 31.29 billion US dollars in 2026, growing at nearly 12% per year. Fashion is one of the primary growth drivers. Online sales will exceed 100 billion riyals this year. This is not a market where you need to convince people to shop online — 99% internet penetration, 78% 5G coverage, 98% mobile penetration. The infrastructure is built. The question is which brands capture the demand. B2C commerce accounts for 73.54% of total e-commerce revenue.

bullets.text: 3rd globally in modest fashion consumption at USD 18B
Women's apparel: USD 13.5B, projected USD 20B by 2034

slides.presenter_notes: Zooming into the modest fashion segment specifically. Saudi Arabia is the third largest modest fashion market globally at 18 billion US dollars. Women's apparel alone is 13.5 billion and growing to 20 billion by 2034 at 4.43% CAGR. E-commerce apparel market is valued at USD 8.59B in 2025, expected to reach USD 16.74B by 2034 at 7.6% CAGR. Online retail is the fastest-growing distribution channel in Saudi fashion. And here is the critical data point for Ein Abayaa: 74.6% of e-commerce buyers are female. The market is enormous, it is growing, and the primary buyer is exactly Ein Abayaa's target customer. Additional points: KSA drives 41% of GCC's USD 80B fashion spend (Fortune).

content.title: BNPL Is Standard, Not Optional
content.label: of Saudi consumers have used Buy Now Pay Later
content.sublabel: BNPL increases AOV by 35%+ and conversion rates by 20-30%

slides.presenter_notes: This is perhaps the single most actionable data point in the entire strategy. 77% of Saudi consumers have used BNPL. It increases average order value by 35% and conversion rates by 20 to 30 percent. 80% of BNPL transactions originate on mobile devices. Apple Pay leads digital wallets at 36% market share, Mada at 22%. Cash on delivery has declined 64% — non-cash payments exceed 75-80% of retail e-commerce. 62% of consumers want BNPL as a standard merchant feature.

content.title: BNPL: Ein Abayaa's Quick Win
content.headline: Tabby + Tamara are active — but per-installment amounts are NOT shown on product pages
bullets: At Maison Ein prices (SAR 514-795), showing '4 payments of SAR 128.50' converts impulse to purchase
Sadal does this best-in-class — prominently displayed on every product page
Must be implemented before Zid store launch

slides.presenter_notes: Ein Abayaa has Tabby and Tamara active, but does NOT display per-installment amounts on product pages. Insight: Showing per-installment amounts is a proven conversion driver — implement before driving paid traffic. For a Maison Ein piece at 600 riyals, showing 'four payments of 150 riyals' is a completely different psychological proposition than showing 600 riyals. Sadal does this best-in-class — Tabby 6 installments plus Tamara 4 installments prominently displayed with exact amounts. This is a quick win that should be implemented before the Zid store launch.

Summer Shade 2026 launches ~April 10, aligned with Eid al-Fitr
Mobile commerce accounts for 75%+ of sales during peak periods

content.title: Mobile-First Is Non-Negotiable
content.label: of online sales happen on mobile in Saudi Arabia
content.sublabel: 34.17M social media users (91.74% of population) spending 3h 6m daily

slides.presenter_notes: Saudi Arabia has 34 million social media users — that is 92% of the population — spending over 3 hours per day, well above the global average of 2 hours 24 minutes. More than 60% use social media to research brands before purchasing. Mobile commerce dominates — over 75% of total online sales happen on mobile. Everything we build must be mobile-first.

For Ein Abayaa, Instagram is the primary channel — 16.3 million users, 43% female, and the number one fashion discovery platform. Ad reach grew by 3.9M in 2023-2024. WhatsApp is the secret weapon — 40 million active users, 98% open rates, and a proven 25% cart recovery rate for Saudi fashion brands. TikTok is the growth play with 49% engagement surge year over year and significantly lower CPMs than Meta. Facebook at 34.5M users (81.39% of social media traffic) is strong for retargeting via the Meta ecosystem. Snapchat at 22-25M users with 90%+ penetration ages 13-34 is a test channel for AR try-on and Gen Z awareness. This is the channel mix we will build the strategy around.

content.title: Sadal — The Value Leader
bullets: Positioning: Volume Saudi abaya retailer on Salla with aggressive discount pricing
Key strength: 82+ reviews per product + BNPL prominently displayed with exact installment amounts
Key weakness: Perpetual discounting, no brand identity — products are numbered (Abaya-16)

slides.presenter_notes: Sadal is the most dangerous competitor, not because of their brand — they have none — but because of their social proof infrastructure. 82+ reviews per product. Exact BNPL installment amounts on every product page — Tabby 6 installments plus Tamara 4 installments. Long-running Meta ads that have been optimizing since August 2024. Dominant by impressions in 'abaya' search. Arabic-only, functional/descriptive language. WhatsApp support active. They compete on price and trust. Ein Abayaa competes on brand and design. But we need to match their trust infrastructure — reviews, BNPL display, WhatsApp support — to close the conversion gap. Basic photography compared to premium competitors.

content.title: Laftah — The Retail Giant
bullets: Positioning: Mass-market brand with 13+ physical stores across 8 cities
Key strength: Physical stores give touch-and-try trust advantage + breakout Google search volume
Key weakness: Poor digital experience — image-only catalog, bad SEO, no brand story
content.threat_level: LOW — different tier, but Google search growth is notable

slides.presenter_notes: Laftah is interesting not because they directly compete with Ein Abayaa — they are a mass-market player with 13 stores across Makkah, Riyadh, Madinah, Jeddah, Abha, Taif, Tabuk, and Jazan — but because they have breakout Google search volume. They are becoming the name people search when they think abaya. Their 13 physical stores give them a trust advantage Ein Abayaa cannot replicate: customers can touch fabric and try before buying. COD plus BNPL plus free shipping over 299 SAR. Customer testimonials with real names. Our response is digital excellence — video fabric close-ups, detailed size guides, and a return policy that removes risk. Heavy reliance on physical retail means their digital feels secondary. Arabic-only with no English language option.

content.title: OYA Abaya — The Platform Peer
bullets: Positioning: Mid-range Saudi brand on Zid (same platform as Ein Abayaa's target)
Key strength: Loyalty program + before/after interactive slider + claims 10K+ customers
Key weakness: Generic Zid template, cluttered homepage, scattered into accessories
content.threat_level: MEDIUM — similar price range, weaker brand identity

slides.presenter_notes: OYA is the closest direct competitor — they are on Zid, in the same price range, and targeting a similar customer. They have some smart features like a loyalty program and before/after slider. Bilingual approach with Arabic primary and English category names. 5-star review display and countdown timer promotions. But their brand identity is weak — they sell shoes, watches, and bags alongside abayas, which dilutes positioning. Ein Abayaa's focused brand architecture — AZAL for everyday, Maison Ein for premium — is a clear strategic advantage over OYA's scattered approach. Product prices were not rendering properly on their site.

content.title: Lagate — The Designer Competitor
bullets: Positioning: Premium/luxury Saudi abaya house with designer Maryam Alsaqqaf
Key strength: Strong storytelling tied to Saudi geography + bilingual execution + BNPL prominent
Key weakness: No visible reviews, limited product count, outdated collection naming
content.threat_level: MEDIUM — Maison Ein competes directly with this price range

slides.presenter_notes: Lagate is the brand most similar to Ein Abayaa in spirit — designer-led, story-driven, premium positioning, bilingual. They do storytelling well, tying their collections to Saudi geography — Red Sea and heritage embroidery narratives. Collection categories include Occasion Abayas, Formal Abayas, Everyday Abayas, and Winter Abayas. Free shipping threshold at 500 SAR versus Laftah's 299. Maison Ein competes directly with their price range. Our advantage is the dual-tier architecture — we serve both the 300-riyal buyer and the 795-riyal buyer. Lagate only serves the premium end. And critically, they have no reviews — same trust gap as everyone except Sadal.

This means Ein Abayaa can capture high-intent buyers — people actively searching for abayas — at low CPCs with virtually no competition. Combined with Sofarah brand term capture, Google becomes a high-efficiency acquisition channel.

slides.presenter_notes: Our influencer strategy is micro and nano-first. The data is clear: micro-influencers deliver the best ROI at 5.78 dollars per dollar spent. Tier two is 5-8 UGC creators per quarter — nano-influencers under 10K followers producing try-on content with full rights for paid repurposing. Tier three is event collaborators — brand partnerships similar to Ein x Base & Boon with premium Saudi lifestyle brands in beauty, wellness, home, and food.
